claim_boundary: This contract fixes the states and mandatory evidence of a plugin on/off display per consumer, host, plugin and scope. It is a schema-level artifact checked against synthetic fixtures. It performs no write, owns no writer and does not claim that any host, consumer or version currently supports activation. A missing source means unknown, never plugged and never unplugged.

observed_from: BACH plugin_sockets flag toggle (read-only analysis: no native write, no read-back, default plugged)
BACH plugin inventory (enabled_in_client per consumer, runtime_active null)
native Claude Code plugin enable/disable with list read-back (read-only analysis)

normative_note: The sections listed in normative_sections (the claim_boundary text included) are pinned by SHA-256 in the checker. Changing any of them (weaker, stronger, reworded) is a new contract version, not an edit. The version step is documented here; the checker accepts only v1 and does not enforce the step independently: a pull request that changes contract and checker together is caught by review, not by this file.

record_fields.note: Unknown fields are rejected. extensions is an object the checker never interprets.

states.name: plugged
states.meaning: The native configuration says enabled, read back from the native source after any write, and no restart is open.

states.name: unplugged
states.meaning: The native configuration says disabled, read back from the native source after any write.

states.name: pending_restart
states.meaning: A change was written (complete write evidence) and read back, but its effect in the running consumer is not evidenced. runtime_active stays null.

states.name: unknown
states.meaning: No native source, not readable, no entry, or a read-back that is not bound to the write. Also the only valid state when the source evidence is missing.

states.name: error
states.meaning: Writing or reading back failed, or the read-back contradicts the request. After a write attempt the reached step and the way back are evidenced.

patterns.note: ASCII only. host is the lowercase form; consumers lowercase a host name before they compare or store it.

known_values.note: Documentation only, not a closed set: a new consumer needs no new contract version. Whether a consumer has a writer is a property of its evidence, not of this list.

write_fields.note: reached_step equals the last entry of steps. A state other than error needs the complete step list. rollback_outcome belongs to error only. A null write block counts as missing.

error_codes.E_SCHEMA: The document schema is not the one of this contract or records is not a list.
error_codes.E_TYPE: A field has the wrong type: text fields are non-empty strings without surrounding whitespace or control characters, flags are exactly true or false, objects and lists only where the contract names them.
error_codes.E_ENUM: A value is outside its enum or does not match its ASCII identifier pattern (consumer, host, plugin_id, source, reason_code, writer_host).
error_codes.E_KEY: A key field (consumer, host, plugin_id, scope) is missing, or the key appears twice.
error_codes.E_STATE: The state is not one of the contract states.
error_codes.E_UNKNOWN_FIELD: A field is not defined for this level of the record. Extensions belong in the extensions object.
error_codes.E_MISSING_EVIDENCE: A mandatory evidence or write field is missing or empty. The code carries the field name.
error_codes.E_HASH: config_revision or readback_sha256 is not 64 hex characters.
error_codes.E_TIME: A timestamp is not extended ISO-8601 with seconds and Z or numeric offset.
error_codes.E_ORDER: requested_at is not strictly before native_write_at, or readback_at lies after observed_at.
error_codes.E_NO_READBACK: plugged, unplugged or pending_restart without readback_ref, readback_at, readback_sha256 or config_revision. Without a bound read-back nothing is plugged or unplugged.
error_codes.E_REVISION_MISMATCH: config_revision differs from readback_sha256, the hash of the content the read-back reference points to.
error_codes.E_STALE_READBACK: readback_at is not strictly after requested_at and native_write_at (earlier or equal). A stale read-back is not evidence; the consumer shows unknown.
error_codes.E_FLAG_ONLY: The source is a flag (for example the plugin_sockets table). A flag is no truth about the native configuration.
error_codes.E_DEFAULT_TRUE: plugged, unplugged or pending_restart is derived from absence or a default (no source, source default or absence, or default_applied true). A missing source must yield unknown.
error_codes.E_FOREIGN_HOST_WRITE: writer_host differs from the host that owns the configuration. A foreign host is display only.
error_codes.E_MISMATCH_NO_ERROR: The requested value differs from the read-back value, or the read-back contradicts the state, but the state is not error.
error_codes.E_PENDING_RUNTIME: pending_restart with runtime_active other than null.
error_codes.E_RUNTIME_NO_REF: runtime_active is true or false without runtime_ref.
error_codes.E_NO_BACKUP: native_write is part of the steps but backup_ref is missing.
error_codes.E_TOGGLE_ORDER: The toggle steps are not the ordered sequence plan, lock_host_check, backup, native_write, readback (complete for a state other than error, an ordered non-empty prefix for error).
error_codes.E_REACHED_STEP: write.reached_step is missing, not a toggle step, or not the last entry of steps.
error_codes.E_WRITE_REQUIRED: pending_restart, or an error in phase write, without a write block (a null write block counts as missing).
error_codes.E_UNKNOWN_NEEDS_REASON: unknown without reason_code, or unknown carrying a read-back value.
error_codes.E_ERROR_NO_ROLLBACK: error after a native write without rollback_outcome (restored, not_needed, failed).

rules.never_without_readback: plugged, unplugged and pending_restart need config_revision, readback_ref, readback_at and readback_sha256 from the native source. Wish is not read-back.
rules.revision_bound_to_readback: config_revision equals readback_sha256, the hash of the content the read-back reference points to. A different hash with an unchanged reference is rejected.
rules.readback_after_write: Every write block carries requested_at. The order is strict: requested_at before native_write_at before readback_at, and readback_at not after observed_at. A read-back that is earlier than or equal to the write is stale and shows unknown.
rules.flag_only_is_no_truth: A flag or table of the display system (plugin_sockets) is never a source for plugged or unplugged.
rules.no_default_true: There is no default state. Missing source or missing entry is unknown. default_applied must be absent or exactly false and cannot lead to plugged.
rules.writer_only_at_data_host: A write is only valid when writer_host equals the host of the record. Other hosts are display only.
rules.toggle_sequence: plan, lock_host_check, backup, native_write, readback, in this order. backup_ref and native_write_at are mandatory once native_write appears.
rules.references_are_structural: readback_ref and the other reference fields are structural text; the checker does not resolve them or compute the hash of the referenced content. The contract is schema-only (see claim_boundary).
rules.write_evidence_complete: pending_restart needs a complete write block. error in phase write needs a write block with reached_step. requested_value and requested_at are mandatory in every write block. A null write block counts as missing.
rules.wish_is_not_readback: If requested_value differs from readback_value, or the read-back contradicts the state, the state must be error.
rules.pending_restart_without_runtime_proof: pending_restart keeps runtime_active null. Only runtime_ref evidence may make runtime_active true or false.
rules.error_evidences_the_way_back: error after a native write carries backup_ref, rollback_outcome and last_evidence.
rules.strict_shape: Unknown fields are rejected, flags are exactly true or false, text fields are non-empty strings without surrounding whitespace, identifiers are ASCII.
rules.open_consumer: consumer is an identifier matching the consumer pattern. Known values are documentation, not a closed enum.
rules.key_unique: The key (consumer, host, plugin_id, scope) appears once per document.

fixtures.note: Every error code has exactly one fixture named neg_<code in lowercase>.json that raises exactly that code. Further negatives are named neg_variant_*.

next_gates: Adapter in the consuming system: endpoint, native writer, lock and backup (P3, owned by that system)
